author: p. b. blankenship
title: Noah Vazquez joins Furman volleyball coaching staff for 2026 season
text:
Furman head volleyball coach Michelle Young announced on June 10 the addition of Noah Vazquez as an assistant coach for the upcoming 2026 season.
Vazquez, originally from Orlando, Florida, arrives in Greenville after serving as Director of Volleyball Operations for the Orlando Valkyries of Major League Volleyball. Young said, “We are excited to welcome Noah to our staff. His passion for developing student-athletes, commitment to excellence, and dedication to building meaningful relationships will make an immediate impact on our program. We look forward to the energy, knowledge, and leadership he will bring to our team.”
During his most recent stint with the Valkyries in 2026, Vazquez oversaw a season where Orlando posted a 13-15 overall record and ended with a three-match winning streak. He previously worked as Volleyball Operations Intern and Practice Player in 2025 when Orlando won the league championship with a 20-10 record by defeating Indy Ignite in the final match.
Vazquez also served as an assistant coach at Rollins College during the 2025 season. The Tars achieved 16 victories that year while player Marta Tsaneva earned third team All-Sunshine State Conference honors after leading Rollins in several statistical categories, including kills and points per set.
His earlier experience includes being part of Timber Creek High School’s coaching staff from 2022-24, where he contributed to a cumulative record of 48-30 and three consecutive FHSAA Regional Tournament appearances—including reaching finals in 2023—and led their junior varsity program during two seasons. On the club circuit since 2023, Vazquez has coached at Oviedo Volleyball Academy.
“I am beyond excited to be joining the staff here at Furman,” Vazquez said. “I’m very grateful to Michelle for the opportunity and look forward to working alongside her, Kelly, and the rest of the staff… I’ve been blessed to have been a part of some very successful teams in the past and look forward to continuing that here at Furman and working to bring some hardware back home to Greenville.” He is also recognized as a former AAU All-American player who won a national championship at age fifteen before graduating from University of Florida in sport management.
